quests.instruction: Which number is the smallest: 612, 955, or 948?
quests.hint: Compare them two at a time, then keep the smaller one.
quests.explanation: Out of 612, 955, and 948, the number 612 is the smallest!
quests.funFact: If you count up by ones, 612 comes right after 611!

quests.instruction: There are 88 groups of ten and 6 more. How many in total?
quests.question: 88 groups of ten and 6 more
quests.hint: Say the group total out loud, then keep counting for the leftover ones.
quests.explanation: 88 groups of ten make 880, plus 6 more makes 886!
quests.funFact: If you count backwards, 886 comes just before 887!

quests.instruction: Read the word and find the matching number!
quests.question: Four Hundred Twenty-Five
quests.hint: Say the word out loud, then look for the matching numeral among the choices.
quests.explanation: "Four Hundred Twenty-Five" is how we say the number 425 in English, so 425 is the digit that matches!
quests.funFact: Double 425 is 850! Because 425 + 425 = 850.

quests.instruction: Which number is the greatest: 993, 987, or 676?
quests.hint: Line all three numbers up in counting order first.
quests.explanation: Out of 993, 987, and 676, the number 993 is the greatest!
quests.funFact: If you add 1 to 993, you get 994!

quests.instruction: What digit is in the hundreds place of 610?
quests.hint: Cover up every digit except the hundreds digit in 610.
quests.explanation: In 610, the digit 6 sits in the hundreds place!
quests.funFact: If you multiply 6 by 10, it becomes 60!

quests.instruction: There are 52 groups of ten and 4 more. How many in total?
quests.question: 52 groups of ten and 4 more
quests.hint: Say the group total out loud, then keep counting for the leftover ones.
quests.explanation: 52 groups of ten make 520, plus 4 more makes 524!
quests.funFact: If you multiply 524 by 10, it becomes 5240!

quests.instruction: Which number is greater: 641 or 539?
quests.question: 641 or 539
quests.hint: Picture counting all the way up -- whichever number you'd reach later is the answer.
quests.explanation: 641 is greater than 539 -- when counting up, 641 comes later!
quests.funFact: If you add 0 to 641, it stays exactly the same: 641!

quests.instruction: There are 63 groups of ten and 4 more. How many in total?
quests.question: 63 groups of ten and 4 more
quests.hint: Say the group total out loud, then keep counting for the leftover ones.
quests.explanation: 63 groups of ten make 630, plus 4 more makes 634!
quests.funFact: The number 634 is an even number!

quests.instruction: What digit is in the tens place of 401?
quests.hint: Count from the right: ones first, then tens, then hundreds -- find the tens spot.
quests.explanation: In 401, the digit 0 sits in the tens place!
quests.funFact: Zero means exactly nothing! If you have 0 apples, you have an empty basket.

quests.instruction: What digit is in the tens place of 741?
quests.hint: Cover up every digit except the tens digit in 741.
quests.explanation: In 741, the digit 4 sits in the tens place!
quests.funFact: If you count backwards, 4 comes just before 5!

quests.instruction: Which number is the greatest: 937, 484, or 495?
quests.hint: The greatest number is the one you'd reach last while counting up from zero.
quests.explanation: Out of 937, 484, and 495, the number 937 is the greatest!
quests.funFact: Double 937 is 1874! Because 937 + 937 = 1874.

quests.instruction: Which number is greater: 424 or 789?
quests.question: 424 or 789
quests.hint: Compare the digits from left to right: which number has more value?
quests.explanation: 789 is greater than 424 -- when counting up, 789 comes later!
quests.funFact: If you add 1 to 789, you get 790!

quests.instruction: Read the word and find the matching number!
quests.question: Four Hundred Seventy-Eight
quests.hint: Sound the word out slowly, then count that many fingers to check.
quests.explanation: "Four Hundred Seventy-Eight" is how we say the number 478 in English, so 478 is the digit that matches!
quests.funFact: If you had 478 apples and found one more, you would have 479 apples!

quests.instruction: Which number is greater: 524 or 709?
quests.question: 524 or 709
quests.hint: Line the numbers up on a number line in your head -- further right is bigger.
quests.explanation: 709 is greater than 524 -- when counting up, 709 comes later!
quests.funFact: If you multiply 709 by 10, it becomes 7090!

quests.instruction: Which number is the greatest: 404, 422, or 574?
quests.hint: The greatest number is the one you'd reach last while counting up from zero.
quests.explanation: Out of 404, 422, and 574, the number 574 is the greatest!
quests.funFact: If you add 0 to 574, it stays exactly the same: 574!

quests.instruction: Which number is greater: 684 or 854?
quests.question: 684 or 854
quests.hint: Line the numbers up on a number line in your head -- further right is bigger.
quests.explanation: 854 is greater than 684 -- when counting up, 854 comes later!
quests.funFact: The number 854 is an even number!

quests.instruction: What number continues the pattern: 0, 25, 50, __?
quests.hint: Look at how much bigger each number is than the one before it -- that jump stays the same every time.
quests.explanation: Each number jumps up by 25, so after 50 comes 50 + 25 = 75!
quests.funFact: The number 75 has two digits: a 7 in the tens place and a 5 in the ones place!

quests.instruction: Look at the number and find the matching word!
quests.hint: Count up to 964 in your head, saying each number word as you go.
quests.explanation: The numeral 964 is written in words as "Nine Hundred Sixty-Four" -- that's its name!
quests.funFact: The digit 4 sits in the ones place of 964, and the digit 6 sits in the tens place!

quests.instruction: Which number is greater: 412 or 734?
quests.question: 412 or 734
quests.hint: Picture counting all the way up -- whichever number you'd reach later is the answer.
quests.explanation: 734 is greater than 412 -- when counting up, 734 comes later!
quests.funFact: If you count backwards, 734 comes just before 735!

quests.instruction: What digit is in the ones place of 671?
quests.hint: Split 671 into its place-value parts, then find the ones part.
quests.explanation: In 671, the digit 1 sits in the ones place!
quests.funFact: If you count backwards, 1 comes just before 2!

quests.instruction: Which number is the greatest: 744, 677, or 863?
quests.hint: Line all three numbers up in counting order first.
quests.explanation: Out of 744, 677, and 863, the number 863 is the greatest!
quests.funFact: If you add 1 to 863, you get 864!

quests.instruction: There are 46 groups of ten and 3 more. How many in total?
quests.question: 46 groups of ten and 3 more
quests.hint: 46 groups of ten is the same as counting by tens 46 times.
quests.explanation: 46 groups of ten make 460, plus 3 more makes 463!
quests.funFact: If you had 463 apples and found one more, you would have 464 apples!

quests.instruction: Which number is greater: 642 or 804?
quests.question: 642 or 804
quests.hint: Picture counting all the way up -- whichever number you'd reach later is the answer.
quests.explanation: 804 is greater than 642 -- when counting up, 804 comes later!
quests.funFact: If you multiply 804 by 10, it becomes 8040!

quests.instruction: Look at the number and find the matching word!
quests.hint: Read the numeral 472 out loud -- what word do you say?
quests.explanation: The numeral 472 is written in words as "Four Hundred Seventy-Two" -- that's its name!
quests.funFact: 472 is an even number -- you could split 472 things into two equal, matching groups!

quests.instruction: Which number is the smallest: 953, 564, or 477?
quests.hint: The smallest number is the one you'd reach first while counting up from zero.
quests.explanation: Out of 953, 564, and 477, the number 477 is the smallest!
quests.funFact: If you add 0 to 477, it stays exactly the same: 477!

quests.instruction: Look at the number and find the matching word!
quests.hint: Count up to 417 in your head, saying each number word as you go.
quests.explanation: The numeral 417 is written in words as "Four Hundred Seventeen" -- that's its name!
quests.funFact: Counting one by one from 1, you would say 417 exactly 417 numbers into your count!

quests.instruction: What number continues the pattern: 10, 60, 110, 160, __?
quests.hint: Look at how much bigger each number is than the one before it -- that jump stays the same every time.
quests.explanation: Each number jumps up by 50, so after 160 comes 160 + 50 = 210!
quests.funFact: The number 210 is an even number!

quests.instruction: Which number is greater: 764 or 870?
quests.question: 764 or 870
quests.hint: Compare the digits from left to right: which number has more value?
quests.explanation: 870 is greater than 764 -- when counting up, 870 comes later!
quests.funFact: If you count up by ones, 870 comes right after 869!

quests.instruction: What digit is in the ones place of 961?
quests.hint: Count from the right: ones first, then tens, then hundreds -- find the ones spot.
quests.explanation: In 961, the digit 1 sits in the ones place!
quests.funFact: The number 1 is a single-digit number, meaning it only takes up one spot!

quests.instruction: What number continues the pattern: 50, 75, 100, 125, __?
quests.hint: Look at how much bigger each number is than the one before it -- that jump stays the same every time.
quests.explanation: Each number jumps up by 25, so after 125 comes 125 + 25 = 150!
quests.funFact: Double 150 is 300! Because 150 + 150 = 300.
